text:
sam-new: Hey folks, starting on-call next week and hitting a few setup snags. My PD invite accepted but when I try to view the runbooks I get a 403 from the docs SSO. Who owns runbook access?

toni-sre: Welcome Sam! :wave: I handle runbook perms. Ping me your LDAP and I'll add you to oncall-readers. Which rotation did you get?

sam-new: I'm on Week A (Pager A) per onboarding email. Also, the staging incident dry-run link in the handbook failed with a 401 when I tried to trigger it.

runbook-bot: Dry-run schedule created: sim-177045 at 2026-05-03T18:00:00Z. This will notify staging only.

toni-sre: 401 likely means your PD token doesn't map to the staging schedule. Steps: accept PD invite, add MFA, then request to join the staging schedule in infra console. I can re-send the schedule invite now.

sam-new: One other: do I need any special SSH or bastion creds for runbook exercises? The runbook mentions `ssh-bastion` role for db incidents.

claire: Bastion creds only for P0 node/db troubleshooting. For the dry-run you'll use simulated db failover in staging; no bastion needed. If you want to practice SSH we can arrange a controlled session.

sam-new: Helpful. Also, what do you expect from the two shadow incidents? Should I create incident notes or just observe?

toni-sre: For first few shadows we want you to do triage and make playbook annotations: set severity, note timeline, and write a short mitigation summary. We'll go through postmortem checklist together.

sam-new: Cool. I tried installing redwoodctl but `curl https://redwood.tools/install.sh | bash` failed with permission denied. Any preferred install method?

toni-sre: We have a homebrew cask now: `brew install redwoodctl`. If you can't use brew, DM infra and they'll push a binary to your workstation.

runbook-bot: Permission change applied: sam -> group:oncall-readers. Temporary access valid 14 days.

sam-new: Confirmed I can open runbooks now. Thanks! Final Q: where's the canonical incident severity doc? The handbook and runbook had slight diffs.

claire: Canonical is the runbook header "Severity definitions (source of truth)". Handbook is summary. If you see mismatches file an issue in `docs/handbook` and tag @ton i-sre.

sam-new: Awesome, feeling better. See you all during the dry-run and shadow sessions. Appreciate the quick fixes!
